⭐️ Michael Saylor says Strategy and Strive can grow together 

🌐 Michael Saylor has argued that Strategy and Strive can compete for investor capital while helping each other expand the market for Bitcoin-backed preferred securities. Under Saylor’s terminology, Bitcoin represents “Digital Capital,” preferred securities such as Strategy’s STRC and Strive’s SATA represent “Digital Credit,” while MSTR and ASST sit in what he calls the “Digital Equity” category. The labels form part of Saylor’s own framework and are not formal regulatory asset classes.

📣 A 0.1% allocation from either pool would equal roughly $160 billion. Michael Saylor used that comparison to argue that Bitcoin treasury companies are competing mainly against much larger traditional equity and fixed-income markets, not only against one another. He wrote that Strategy and Strive may compete for the same individual investment, but a new investor learning how to assess one Bitcoin-linked preferred security could become more comfortable evaluating another. Saylor said several credible issuers could bring more research, trading liquidity and institutional attention to the category.

⚠️ The two companies remain separate businesses with different securities, liabilities and management decisions. Strategy issues STRC, while Strive issues SATA. Both are perpetual preferred securities, but their terms and dividend schedules differ. Strive said the purchase extended its SATA dividend reserve to 18 months, consisting at the time of 12 months of cash and another six months represented by STRC at prevailing market prices. The company described STRC as part of its reserve strategy, while stressing that market values can change.

➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

The race is on, and people have already minted many beautiful numbers from various masks and special collections, although only 26% of the total supply has been minted.

On average, 117 4N domains are minted per day. At the current rate, 50% of the supply will be minted by March 22, 2026, 75% by April 12, 2026, and 100% by May 4, 2026. 

Why 4N domains if there are already Telegram usernames?

1. Numbers are the international language of communication. They are simple and understandable for everyone around the world, unlike various alphabets (be it Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic, hieroglyphs, etc.).

2. There are 10^4 = 10,000 number combinations in 4N domains, compared to 26^4 = 456,976 combinations in alphabetical ones.

3. The price for the 4L username is fixed at $8,000. The price for the 4N domain on mint is approximately $130, which is 61.54 times cheaper!

4. Only domains can consist of numbers, while usernames must contain at least one letter. Therefore, 4N domains are beyond competition in the TON ecosystem.

5. The ability to associate attractive domain digits with a gift number. An example is here. There are dozens of different collections of gifts with identical numbers, but only one 4N domain can be associated with them!

6. The TON ecosystem will have thousands of AI agents, and they will need a short digital domain for convenience.

7. TON Browser and TON Messenger are being developed, with user login via TON DNS.

⚡️ ‘Don’t let my friends be forgotten’: Surviving Minab student writes to Araghchi

📌 Tehran, IRNA - Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Sunday he has received a letter from a surviving student of the Shajareh Tayyebah School in Minab, which came under a deadly US missile attack late in February, and published its text in an Instagram message.

“Today, on the sidelines of the international conference ‘Ecocide: The Silent War Crime,’ I received a letter from Fatemeh-Zahra Sheikh-Abadi, a surviving student of the Shajareh Tayyebah School in Minab,” Araghchi wrote in the message.
​
Araghchi said that in the letter, she remembers her friends and classmates—Niayesh, Sonaz, Baran, and Zeinab—children who were martyred in the US attack on the Shajareh Tayyebah School in Minab on February 28.
​
Fatemeh-Zahra wrote that she survived to speak about her friends and keep their memory alive, the foreign minister noted.
​
She also asks the United Nations why it does not act against this catastrophe and in support of children’s rights, and calls on the Iranian people not to let her friends be forgotten, he added.
​
“For me and my colleagues at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, receiving this letter is a responsibility beyond sympathy for the martyred children of Minab; our real responsibility is to record the truth, pursue the legal and international dimensions of this crime, and hold the perpetrators and those who ordered it accountable,” Araghchi added.
​
The foreign minister noted, “The names of the children of Minab and Lamerd should not remain alive only in memories; these names must also endure in the path of seeking justice.”
​
“I consider it my duty to convey Fatemeh-Zahra’s voice and the narrative of the children of Minab to international fora and not allow the passage of time to marginalize the truth of this catastrophe and the necessity of accountability for it.”
​
On the first day of the aggression against Iran, the US military attacked the Minab Elementary School, killing 168 innocent people, including students, sports players, school board members, teachers, and parents.

Something happened in the U.S. Treasury market that’s hard to ignore.

The quarter closed with 20-year Treasury yields at 5.68% and 30-year yields at 5.64%. These are levels the market hasn’t seen in more than 20 years. And this is no longer just a random spike lasting a couple of days, but a very noticeable shift in the cost of long-term borrowing.

Why are yields rising? Investors want an increasingly larger premium for lending money to the U.S. government for decades. The reasons are clear. Massive government debt, a large budget deficit, inflation that remains elevated, and a huge amount of new borrowing. In other words, the market is demanding an increasingly higher price for long-term U.S. debt.

And here’s the key question. What happens if 5% or 6% turn out not to be the ceiling, and yields eventually climb to 8%, 9%, or even 10%? For now, that’s not the base-case scenario, but if it happens, the rules of the game in financial markets will change dramatically.

Because when U.S. government bond yields hit 8%, investors face a simple question. Why take on significant risk in stocks, crypto, real estate, or gold when you can earn that kind of return in dollars from one of the most reliable financial instruments in the world? At that point, some capital could start flowing into Treasuries, and all other asset classes would have to offer significantly higher potential returns to remain attractive.

My takeaway is simple. Right now, it’s important to watch not just stocks and crypto, but the bond market as well. If the era of cheap money really is over, long-term Treasuries could become one of the key indicators of where global capital is headed next.
